subtopic: Definition of a Limit and One-Sided Limits
stem: Consider the example \(f(x) = 3x + 1\), take \(a = 0\) and \(l = 1\). Verify the \(\varepsilon\)-\(\delta\) definition of the limit, i.e. find \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - 0| < \delta\) implies \(|f(x) - l| < \varepsilon\).
solution:
We want to find some \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - 0| < \delta\) implies that \(|(3x + 1) - 1| < \varepsilon\)

if \(|3x| < \varepsilon\)  i.e. if \(3|x| < \varepsilon\)  i.e. if \(|x| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{3}\)

So, we can choose \(\delta = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{3}\)

(In fact any \(\delta \le \dfrac{\varepsilon}{3}\) will do.)

\(\therefore\ 0 < |x - 0| < \delta \Rightarrow |f(x) - l| < \varepsilon\)

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 0} (3x + 1) = 1\)
_note: Printed stem is only 'Consider the example f(x) = 3x + 1, take a = 0 and l = 1'; the instruction to verify the definition comes from the block's shared lead-in 'Strategy : Steps for verifying the ∈ - δ definition' printed above Ex. 1 — folded into the stem here so the question is self-contained. The book prints the set-membership glyph '∈' throughout this chapter where epsilon is meant (it prints a genuine ε in Ex. 6 of the 7.1.7 block, confirming the intent); transcribed as \varepsilon. The book also misprints 'If fact any δ ≤ ∈/3 will do' for 'In fact'. Fig. 7.2 sits below this example illustrating the band 1−∈ < y < 1+∈; it is illustrative and the example is answerable without it.

subtopic: Definition of a Limit and One-Sided Limits
stem: \(f(x) = x^2\). Here take \(a = 3\) and \(l = 9\). Find \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - 3| < \delta\) implies \(|x^2 - 9| < \varepsilon\).
solution:
We want to find some \(\delta > 0\) such that \(0 < |x - 3| < \delta\) implies \(|x^2 - 9| < \varepsilon\)

i.e. \(3 - \delta < x < 3 + \delta \Rightarrow |x^2 - 9| < \varepsilon\)

\(\delta\) can be chosen as small as we like and take \(\delta < 1\)

Then, \(3 - \delta < x < 3 + \delta \Rightarrow 2 < x < 4\) or \(5 < x + 3 < 7\)

We want \(|(x + 3)(x - 3)| < \varepsilon\)

But \(|(x + 3)(x - 3)| < 7|x - 3|\)

So \(7|(x - 3)| < \varepsilon \Rightarrow |x^2 - 9| < \varepsilon\)

If \(\delta = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{7}\), \(|(x - 3)| < \delta \Rightarrow |x^2 - 9| < \varepsilon\)

So we choose \(\delta = \min\left\{\dfrac{\varepsilon}{7}, 1\right\}\)

then \(|(x - 3)| < \delta \Rightarrow |f(x) - 9| < \varepsilon\)

* Note that, we want to get rid of factor \(|x + 3|\). Hence we have to get its lower bound.
_note: The book's closing note says we must get the 'lower bound' of |x + 3|; to bound the product |x+3||x−3| ABOVE the argument actually uses an UPPER bound (|x + 3| < 7, from 5 < x + 3 < 7). The derivation itself is correct — only the word is wrong.

stem: \(f(x) = [x]\), \(2 < x < 4\), where \([x]\) is the greatest integer function. Study the limits of \(f(x)\) as \(x \to 3\) and as \(x \to 2.7\).
solution:
We have seen the \(f(x) = [x]\), \(2 \le x \le 4\)

Note that \([x] = 2\) for \(2 \le x < 3\)

\(= 3\) for \(3 \le x < 4\)

Let us study the limits of \(f(x)\) as \(x \to 3\) and \(x \to 2.7\)

\(\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = 3\),

But for \(x < 3\), \(f(x) = 2\). So, \(\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = 2\).

If we take \(l = 3\), then for \(\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and any \(\delta > 0\)

\(3 - \delta < x < 3 \Rightarrow f(x) = 2\) and \(|f(x) - l| = 1 \not< \varepsilon\)

If we take \(l = 2\), then \(3 < x < 3 + \delta \Rightarrow f(x) = 3\),

\(|f(x) - 2| = 1 \not< \varepsilon\)

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 3} f(x)\) does not exist.

Consider \(\lim_{x \to 2.7} f(x)\)

Consider \(a = 2.7\). We see that for \(2 < x < 3\), \(f(x) = 2\).

If we choose \(\delta = 0.3\),

then \(2 < 2.7 - \delta < 2.7 < 2.7 + \delta < 3\)

and \(f(x) = 2\) is a constant.

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 2.7} f(x) = 2\)
_note: Two printed inconsistencies. (1) The stem states the domain as 2 < x < 4 while the very next line of the solution restates it as 2 ≤ x ≤ 4. (2) With δ = 0.3 the chain '2.7 + δ < 3' reads 3 < 3, which is false as a strict inequality; any δ < 0.3 (or reading the interval as open) makes the argument correct, and the conclusion lim = 2 is right either way.

subtopic: Definition of a Limit and One-Sided Limits
stem:
Find left hand limit and right hand limit for the following function.

\(f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x + 1 & \text{if } x < 1 \\ 7x^2 - 3 & \text{if } x \ge 1 \end{cases}\)
solution:
Right hand limit, \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\), for \(x > 1\)

i.e. \(\lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1} (7x^2 - 3) = 4\)

Left hand limit, \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)\), for \(x < 1\):

\(\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1} (3x + 1) = 4\)

Since left and right-hand limits are equal, the two-sided limit is defined, and \(\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = 4\).
_note: Printed as an unnumbered 'Example:' immediately after §7.1.6 (Existence of a limit of a function at a point x = a), with its own 'Solution :' — it carries no 'Ex. n' label, hence the ref number 1 assigned here.

solution:
\(\lim_{n \to 3} \left( \sum_{r=1}^{n} r^2 \right) = \lim_{n \to 3} \left( \dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} \right)\)

\(= \dfrac{(3) \times (3+1) \times (6+1)}{6}\)

\(= \dfrac{3 \times 4 \times 7}{6}\)

\(= 14\)

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 3} \left( \dfrac{\sqrt{6 + x} - \sqrt{7 - x}}{x} \right) = \dfrac{\lim_{x \to 3} \left( \sqrt{6 + x} \right) - \lim_{x \to 3} \left( \sqrt{7 - x} \right)}{\lim_{x \to 3} (x)}\)

\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{6 + 3} - \sqrt{7 - 3}}{3}\)

\(= \dfrac{\sqrt{9} - \sqrt{4}}{3} = \dfrac{3 - 2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
_note: The book's final step prints \(\frac{3-2}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\); the value of \(\frac{3-2}{3}\) is \(\frac{1}{3}\), not \(\frac{1}{2}\). Transcribed as printed.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 1} \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{x} - 1}{x - 1} \right) = \lim_{x \to 1} \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{1 - x}{x}}{x - 1} \right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 1} \left[ \dfrac{(1 - x)}{(x - 1) \times x} \right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 1} \left[ \dfrac{-(x - 1)}{(x - 1) \times x} \right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 1} \left[ \dfrac{-1}{x} \right]\)  \(\left[ \text{As } x \to 1,\ x - 1 \ne 0 \right]\)

\(= -\lim_{x \to 1} \left[ \dfrac{1}{x} \right] = -\dfrac{1}{1}\)

\(= -1\)

subtopic: Definition of a Limit and One-Sided Limits
stem:
Discuss the limit of the following function as \(x\) tends to 3 if

\(f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2 + x + 1, & 2 \le x \le 3 \\ 2x + 1, & 3 < x \le 4 \end{cases}\)
solution:
As \(f(x)\) is defined seperately for \(x \le 3\) and \(x > 3\), we have to find left hand limit (when \(x \le 3\)) and right hand limit (when \(x > 3\)) to discuss the existance of limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x \to 3\).

For the interval \(2 \le x \le 3\); \(f(x) = x^2 + x + 1\)

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^-} (x^2 + x + 1) = (3)^2 + 3 + 1\)

\(= 9 + 3 + 1 = 13\)   -----(I)

Similarly for the interval \(3 < x \le 4\); \(f(x) = 2x + 1\)

\(\lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 3^+} (2x + 1) = (2 \times 3) + 1\)

\(= 6 + 1 = 7\)   -----(II)

From (I) and (II), \(\lim_{x \to 3^-} f(x) \ne \lim_{x \to 3^+} f(x)\)

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 3} f(x)\) does not exist.
_note: The book prints 'seperately' and 'existance'; transcribed as printed.

stem: For a given \(\varepsilon > 0\), find \(\delta > 0\) such that whenever \(|x - a| < \delta\), we have \(|f(x) - l| < \varepsilon\) so that \(\lim_{x \to 1} (4x + 3) = 7\)
solution:
We want to find \(\delta\) so that \(\lim_{x \to 1} (4x + 3) = 7\)

Here \(a = 1\), \(l = 7\) and \(f(x) = 4x + 3\)

Consider \(\varepsilon > 0\) and \(|f(x) - l| < \varepsilon\)

\(|(4x + 3) - 7| < \varepsilon\)

if \(|(4x - 4)| < \varepsilon\)

i.e. if \(|4(x - 1)| < \varepsilon\)

i.e. if \(|x - 1| < \dfrac{\varepsilon}{4}\)

We can have \(\delta \le \dfrac{\varepsilon}{4}\) so that \(|(x - 1)| < \delta \Rightarrow |f(x) - 7| < \varepsilon\)

\(\lim_{x \to 5} \left( \dfrac{x^4 - 625}{x - 5} \right) = \lim_{x \to 5} \left( \dfrac{x^4 - 5^4}{x - 5} \right)\)

\(= 4(5)^{4-1}\)  \(\ldots \left[ \because \lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^n - a^n}{x - a} = na^{n-1} \right]\)

\(= 4(125) = 500\)

\(\lim_{x \to 2} \left( \dfrac{x^7 - 128}{x^5 - 32} \right) = \lim_{x \to 2} \left( \dfrac{x^7 - 2^7}{x^5 - 2^5} \right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 2} \left( \dfrac{\dfrac{x^7 - 2^7}{x - 2}}{\dfrac{x^5 - 2^5}{x - 2}} \right)\)  \(\ldots \left[ \text{As } x \to 2,\ x - 2 \ne 0 \right]\)

\(= \dfrac{7(2)^6}{5(2)^4}\)  \(\ldots \left[ \because \lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{x^n - a^n}{x - a} = na^{n-1} \right]\)

\(= \dfrac{7(2)^2}{5}\)

\(= \dfrac{28}{5}\)
_note: Misprint in the printed solution: the third line (the compound-fraction step) is labelled \(\lim_{x \to 5}\) where it must be \(\lim_{x \to 2}\) — every other line of the example, and its own bracketed remark 'As x→2, x − 2 ≠ 0', use x→2. The value 28/5 is correct.

solution:
Given \(\lim_{x \to 4} \left[ \dfrac{x^n - 4^n}{x - 4} \right] = 48\)

\(\therefore\ n(4)^{n-1} = 48\)

\(\therefore\ n(4)^{n-1} = 3(4)^{3-1}\)

\(\therefore\ n = 3\)  \(\ldots\) by comparing

Put \(26 + x = t^3\), \(\therefore x = t^3 - 26\)

As \(x \to 1\), \(t \to 3\)

\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to 1} \left[ \dfrac{2x - 2}{\sqrt[3]{26 + x} - 3} \right] = \lim_{t \to 3} \left[ \dfrac{2(t^3 - 26) - 2}{\sqrt[3]{t^3} - 3} \right]\)

\(= \lim_{t \to 3} \left[ \dfrac{2(t^3 - 3^3)}{t - 3} \right]\)

\(= 2 \lim_{t \to 3} \left[ \dfrac{t^3 - 3^3}{t - 3} \right]\)

\(= 2 \times 3(3)^{3-1}\)

\(= 54\)

solution:
If we substitute \(z = 3\) in numerator and denominator, we get \(z(2z-3)-9 = 0\) and \(z^{2}-4z+3 = 0\)
So \((z-3)\) is a factor in the numerator and denominator.
\(\lim_{z \to 3}\left[\dfrac{z(2z-3)-9}{z^{2}-4z+3}\right] = \lim_{z \to 3}\left[\dfrac{2z^{2}-3z-9}{z^{2}-4z+3}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 3}\left[\dfrac{(z-3)(2z+3)}{(z-3)(z-1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 3}\left[\dfrac{(2z+3)}{(z-1)}\right]\) ...[As \(z \to 3\), \(z-3 \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{2(3)+3}{3-1}\)
\(= \dfrac{9}{2}\)

\(\lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{1}{x-1}+\dfrac{2}{(1-x)(x+1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{1}{x-1}-\dfrac{2}{(x-1)(x+1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{1+x-2}{(x-1)(x+1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{x-1}{(x-1)(x+1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{1}{(x+1)}\right]\) ...[As \(x \to 1\), \(x-1 \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\)

In this case \((x-1)\) is a factor of the numerator and denominator
To find another factor we use synthetic division.
Numerator: \(x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+3\)

| 1 | 1 | 1 | -5 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  |  | 1 | 2 | -3 |
|  | 1 | 2 | -3 | 0 |

\(\therefore x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+3 = (x-1)\left(x^{2}+2x-3\right)\)
Denominator: \(x^{2}-1 = (x+1)(x-1)\)
\(\lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{x^{3}+x^{2}-5x+3}{x^{2}-1}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{(x-1)\left(x^{2}+2x-3\right)}{(x+1)(x-1)}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 1}\left[\dfrac{x^{2}+2x-3}{x+1}\right]\) ...[As \(x \to 1\), \(x-1 \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{1+2-3}{1+1} = 0\)

_note: Denominator transcribed as printed: \(x^{2}-1\), verified at 5x zoom. Note this is NOT a 0/0 form (at x=2 it is 0/3), so it needs no factorization at all, which is out of character for a Method-of-Factorization exercise; a misprint for \(x^{2}-4\) is plausible. The printed key (0) does not discriminate - both readings give 0 - so no repair is made here.

Stem verified at 5x zoom exactly as printed. SUSPECTED BOOK ANSWER-KEY ERROR (sign): the printed key gives -2, but the expression simplifies to \(\dfrac{x-3}{x(x-2)}\) (since \((x-2)^{2}-1=(x-1)(x-3)\)), whose value at \(x=1\) is \(\dfrac{-2}{-1}=+2\); a numerical check at \(x=1.001\) gives 1.999. Flagged for the cross-check pass; nothing repaired.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x}-1}{x}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x}-1}{x} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{1+x}+1}{\sqrt{1+x}+1}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1+x-1}{x\left(\sqrt{1+x}+1\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{x}{x\left(\sqrt{1+x}+1\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+x}+1}\right)\) ...[As \(x \to 0\), \(x \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+0}+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)
_note: The book prints the label as "Soluton :" (misspelt) for this example only.

solution:
\(\lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{(b+z)^{\frac{1}{2}}-(b-z)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{z}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{b+z}-\sqrt{b-z}}{z}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{b+z}-\sqrt{b-z}}{z} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{b+z}+\sqrt{b-z}}{\sqrt{b+z}+\sqrt{b-z}}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{(b+z)-(b-z)}{z} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{b+z}+\sqrt{b-z}}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{2z}{z} \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{b+z}+\sqrt{b-z}}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{z \to 0}\left[\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{b+z}+\sqrt{b-z}}\right]\) ...[As \(z \to 0\), \(z \ne 0\)]
\(= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{b+0}+\sqrt{b-0}}\)
\(= \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{b}}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{b}}\)

_note: The stem and the first five lines of this solution are printed on p-09 (printed p.142); the working is completed at the top of the left column of p-10 (printed p.143).

stem: If \(3x^2 + 2 \le f(x) \le 5x^2 - 6\) for all \(x \in R\), then find \(\lim_{x \to -2} f(x)\).
solution:
Let \(g(x) = 3x^2 + 2\) and \(h(x) = 5x^2 - 6\)
So, we have \(g(x) \le f(x) \le h(x)\)
Taking as limit \(x \to -2\) throughout we get
\(\lim_{x \to -2} g(x) \le \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) \le \lim_{x \to -2} h(x)\)
\(\lim_{x \to -2}(3x^2 + 2) \le \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) \le \lim_{x \to -2}(5x^2 - 6)\)
\(3(-2)^2 + 2 \le \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) \le 5(-2)^2 - 6\)
\(14 \le \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) \le 14\)
\(\therefore\ \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) = 14\) ....... [By squeeze theorem]
_note: Sits inside section 7.4 (Limit of a trigonometric function), where the book states the squeeze/sandwich theorem as the tool used to prove \(\lim_{\theta\to0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}=1\). The question itself is purely polynomial, so the subtopic is a section-placement call rather than a content match; no canonical subtopic covers the squeeze theorem.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{\cot x - 1}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 x - 2}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{\cot x - 1}{\cot^2 x + 1 - 2}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{\cot x - 1}{\cot^2 x - 1}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{\cot x - 1}{(\cot x + 1)(\cot x - 1)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{1}{\cot x + 1}\right)\) .....[As \(x \to \frac{\pi}{4}\), \(\cot x - 1 \ne 0\)]
\(= \frac{1}{\cot\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) + 1} = \frac{1}{1 + 1}\)
\(= \frac{1}{2}\)
_note: The bracketed remark is printed as "[As x  \(\frac{\pi}{4}\)  cot x \(-\) 1 \(\ne\) 0]" — the arrow after x is missing on the printed page. Transcribed here with the arrow restored, as the intent is unambiguous.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3 - \sin x} - 2}{\cos^2 x}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3 - \sin x} - 2}{\cos^2 x} \times \frac{\sqrt{3 - \sin x} + 2}{\sqrt{3 - \sin x} + 2}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{3 - \sin x - 4}{\cos^2 x\left(\sqrt{3 - \sin x} + 2\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{-1 - \sin x}{1 - \sin^2 x\left(\sqrt{3 - \sin x} + 2\right)}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}}\left(\frac{-(1 + \sin x)}{(1 - \sin x)(1 + \sin x)\left(\sqrt{3 - \sin x} + 2\right)}\right)\)
.....As \(x \to \frac{3\pi}{2}\), \(\sin x \to -1\) and \(1 + \sin x \ne 0\)
\(= \left(\frac{-1}{\left(1 - \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\right)\left(\sqrt{3 - \sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)} + 2\right)}\right)\)
\(= \frac{-1}{(1 + 1)\left(\sqrt{3 + 1} + 2\right)} = -\frac{1}{8}\)
_note: In the fourth line the book prints the denominator as \(1-\sin^2 x\left(\sqrt{3-\sin x}+2\right)\) with the \(1-\sin^2 x\) not bracketed; the intended (and next-line) form is \(\left(1-\sin^2 x\right)\left(\sqrt{3-\sin x}+2\right)\). Transcribed as printed.

solution:
\(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin 7\theta}{\theta}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin 7\theta}{7\theta}\right] \times 7\)
... as \(\theta \to 0\), \(7\theta \to 0\)
\(= 1 \times 7\)  \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin p\theta}{p\theta} = 1\right]\)
\(= 7\)

\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin 8x}{\tan 4x}\right]\)
Divide Numerator and Denominator by \(x\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{\sin 8x}{x}}{\dfrac{\tan 4x}{x}}\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\sin 8x}{x}\right]}{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\tan 4x}{x}\right]}\)
\(= \dfrac{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\sin 8x}{8x} \times 8\right]}{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\tan 4x}{4x} \times 4\right]}\)
\(= \frac{1 \times 8}{1 \times 4} = 2\)  (... as \(x \to 0\), \(8x \to 0\), \(4x \to 0\))
.... \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin p\theta}{p\theta}\right) = 1\), \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\tan p\theta}{p\theta}\right) = 1\)

\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{2\sin x - \sin 2x}{x^3}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{2\sin x - 2\sin x \cdot \cos x}{x^3}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{2\sin x(1 - \cos x)}{x \cdot x^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{2\sin x}{x}\right] \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{1 - \cos x}{x^2}\right]\)
\(= 2 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right] \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{1 - \cos x}{x^2} \times \frac{1 + \cos x}{1 + \cos x}\right]\)
\(= 2 \times 1 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{x^2} \times \frac{1}{1 + \cos x}\right]\)
\(= 2 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin^2 x}{x^2}\right] \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{1}{1 + \cos x}\right]\)
\(= 2 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x}{x}\right]^2 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{1}{1 + \cos 0}\right]\)
\(= 2(1)^2 \times \left[\frac{1}{1 + 1}\right]\)  \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1\right]\)
\(= 2 \times 1 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\)

\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x^2\left(1 - \cos x^2\right)}{x^6}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x^2\left(1 - \cos x^2\right)}{x^6} \times \frac{1 + \cos x^2}{1 + \cos x^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x^2\left(1 - \cos^2 x^2\right)}{x^6} \times \frac{1}{1 + \cos x^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x^2 \cdot \sin^2 x^2}{x^6} \times \frac{1}{1 + \cos x^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin^3 x^2}{\left(x^2\right)^3} \times \frac{1}{1 + \cos x^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{x^2 \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin x^2}{x^2}\right]^3 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{1}{1 + \cos x^2}\right)\)
.....[As \(x \to 0\), \(x^2 \to 0\)]
\(= (1)^3\ \frac{1}{1 + \cos 0} = \frac{1}{1 + 1} = \frac{1}{2}\)
..... \(\left[\lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}\right) = 1,\ here\ \theta = x^2\right]\)

\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\cos 5x^{\circ} - \cos 3x^{\circ}}{x^2}\right)\)
\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{-2\sin 4x^{\circ}\sin x^{\circ}}{x^2}\right)\)
\(= -2\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin 4x^{\circ}}{x} \times \frac{\sin x^{\circ}}{x}\right)\)
\(= -2\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin 4\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right)}{x} \times \frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right)}{x}\right)\)
\(= -2\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{45}\right)}{x} \times \frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right)}{x}\right)\)
\(= -2\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{45}\right)}{\frac{\pi x}{45}}\right) \times \frac{\pi}{45} \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{180}\right)}{\frac{\pi x}{180}}\right) \times \frac{\pi}{180}\)
\(= -2 \times (1) \times \frac{\pi}{45} \times (1) \times \frac{\pi}{180}\) ...... \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin p\theta}{p\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(= -2 \times 4 \times \frac{\pi}{180} \times \frac{\pi}{180} = -8\left(\frac{\pi}{180}\right)^2\)

Put \(x - \frac{\pi}{2} = t\)  \(\therefore x = \frac{\pi}{2} + t\)
As \(x \to \frac{\pi}{2}\); \(t \to 0\).
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{2}}\left[\frac{\cos x}{x - \frac{\pi}{2}}\right] = \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + t\right)}{t}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{-\sin t}{t}\right]\)
\(= -\lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin t}{t}\right]\)
\(= -1\)  \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)

Put \(x - a = t\)  \(\therefore x = a + t\);
As \(x \to a\), \(t \to 0\).
\(\lim_{x \to a}\left[\frac{\cos x - \cos a}{x - a}\right] = \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\cos(a + t) - \cos a}{t}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{-2\sin\left(\frac{2a + t}{2}\right) \cdot \sin\frac{t}{2}}{t}\right]\)
\(= 2\lim_{t \to 0}\left[-\sin\left(a + \frac{t}{2}\right) \cdot \frac{\sin(t/2)}{t}\right]\)
\(= -2\lim_{t \to 0}\left[\sin\left(a + \frac{t}{2}\right)\right]\lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin(t/2)}{t/2}\right]\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
\(= -2\sin(a + 0) \cdot (1)\ \frac{1}{2}\) .... \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin \theta}{\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(= -\sin a\)

Put \(1 - x = t\)  \(\therefore x = 1 - t\);
As \(x \to 1\), \(t \to 0\).
\(\lim_{x \to 1}\left[\frac{1 + \cos \pi x}{(1 - x)^2}\right] = \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{1 + \cos[\pi(1 - t)]}{t^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{1 + \cos(\pi - \pi t)}{(1 - x)^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{1 - \cos \pi t}{t^2}\right]\)
\(= \lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{2\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)}{t^2}\right]\)
\(= 2\lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)}{t}\right]^2\)
\(= 2\lim_{t \to 0}\left[\frac{\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)}{\frac{\pi t}{2}}\right]^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)^2\)
\(= 2(1)\left(\frac{\pi^2}{4}\right)\) .... \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\frac{\sin P\theta}{P\theta}\right) = 1\right]\)
\(= \frac{\pi^2}{2}\)
_note: Book misprint in the printed solution: the second line of the chain carries the denominator \((1-x)^2\), which should be \(t^2\) — the substitution has already been made on the line above and is used again on the line below. Transcribed as printed.

solution:
Put \(\frac{\pi}{3} - x = t\),  \(\therefore x = \frac{\pi}{3} - t\),
As \(x \to \frac{\pi}{3}\), \(t \to 0\)
\(\lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{3}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \tan x}{\pi - 3x}\right) = \lim_{x \to \frac{\pi}{3}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \tan}{3\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - x\right)}\right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - t\right)}{t}\right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \frac{\tan(\pi/3) - \tan t}{1 + \tan(\pi/3)\tan t}}{t}\right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3} - \tan t}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan t}}{t}\right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{\frac{\sqrt{3} + 3\tan t - \sqrt{3} + \tan t}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan t}}{t}\right)\)
\(= \frac{1}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{4\tan t}{t(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan t)}\right)\)
\(= \frac{4}{3}\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{\tan t}{t}\right)\lim_{t \to 0}\left(\frac{1}{1 + \sqrt{3}\tan t}\right)\)
\(= \frac{4}{3}(1) \times \frac{1}{\left(1 + \sqrt{3}\tan 0\right)}\) ....... \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\tan \theta}{\theta} = 1\right]\)
\(= \frac{4}{3}\)
_note: Book misprint in the printed solution: the first line of the chain prints \(\sqrt{3}-\tan\) in the numerator with the argument \(x\) dropped. Transcribed as printed.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{5^{x} - 1}{\sin x}\right]\)

Divide Numerator and Denominator by \(x\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{5^{x} - 1}{x}}{\dfrac{\sin x}{x}}\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{5^{x} - 1}{x}\right]}{\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right]}\)

\(= \dfrac{\log 5}{1}\)

.... \(\left[\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\theta}\right) = 1,\ \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{a^{x} - 1}{x}\right) = \log a\right]\)

\(= (\log 5)\)

subtopic: Limits of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
solution:
Given \(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{5^{x} - 3^{x}}{x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{5^{x} - 1 - 3^{x} + 1}{x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\left(5^{x} - 1\right) - \left(3^{x} - 1\right)}{x}\right]\)

\(= \log 5 - \log 3\) ..... \(\lim_{x \to a}\left(\dfrac{a^{x} - 1}{x}\right) = \log a\)

\(= \log\left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)\)
_note: Book misprint in the printed solution's citation: the standard result is quoted as \(\lim_{x \to a}\left(\frac{a^x-1}{x}\right)=\log a\); the limit should be \(x \to 0\) (the same result is printed correctly with \(x \to 0\) in the SolvedEx.1 citation and in §7.6 result 2). Transcribed as printed.

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{3x + 2}{2 - 5x}\right]^{\frac{1}{3x}} = \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{2 + 3x}{2 - 5x}\right]^{\frac{1}{3x}}\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{2\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)}{2\left(1 - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)}\right]^{\frac{1}{3x}}\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{x}}}{\left(1 - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{x}}}\right]^{\frac{1}{3}}\)

\(= \dfrac{\left[\lim_{x \to 0}\left(1 + \dfrac{3x}{2}\right)^{\frac{2}{3x}}\right]^{\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}}}{\left[\lim_{x \to 0}\left(1 + \dfrac{-5x}{2}\right)^{\frac{2}{-5x}}\right]^{\frac{-5}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}}}\)

\(= \dfrac{e^{\frac{3}{6}}}{e^{\frac{-5}{6}}}\) ..... \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}(1 + kx)^{\frac{1}{kx}} = e\right]\)

\(= e^{\frac{8}{6}} = e^{\frac{4}{3}}\)

subtopic: Limits of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log 4 + \log(0.25 + x)}{x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log\left[4(0.25 + x)\right]}{x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log(1 + 4x)}{x}\right]\)

\(= 4 \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log(1 + 4x)}{4x}\right]\)

\(= 4(1)\) ..... \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\log(1 + px)}{px}\right] = 1\right]\)

\(= 4\)

subtopic: Limits of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{e^{2x} + e^{-2x} - 2}{x \sin x}\right) = \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{e^{2x}\left(e^{2x} + e^{-2x} - 2\right)}{e^{2x}\, x \sin x}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{e^{4x} + 1 - 2e^{2x}}{e^{2x}\, x \sin x}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\left(e^{2x}\right)^{2} - 2e^{2x} + 1}{e^{2x}\, x \sin x}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\left(e^{2x} - 1\right)^{2}}{x \sin x} \times \dfrac{1}{e^{2x}}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{\left(e^{2x} - 1\right)^{2}}{x^{2}}}{\dfrac{x \sin x}{x^{2}}} \times \dfrac{1}{e^{2x}}\right)\)

.... [As \(x \to 0,\ x \ne 0,\ x^{2} \ne 0\)]

\(= \dfrac{\left[\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{e^{2x} - 1}{2x}\right)\right]^{2} \times 4}{\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right)} \times \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{e^{2x}}\right)\)

\(= \dfrac{(1)^{2} \times 4}{1} \times \dfrac{1}{e^{0}}\) ..... \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{e^{kx} - 1}{kx} = 1,\ \lim_{\theta \to 0}\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\right]\)

\(= 4\)

subtopic: Limits of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
solution:
\(\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{21^{x} - 7^{x} - 3^{x} + 1}{x \log(1 + x)}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{7^{x} \cdot 3^{x} - 7^{x} - 3^{x} + 1}{x \log(1 + x)}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{7^{x}\left(3^{x} - 1\right) - \left(3^{x} - 1\right)}{x \log(1 + x)}\right)\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\left(3^{x} - 1\right)\left(7^{x} - 1\right)}{x \log(1 + x)}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{\left(3^{x} - 1\right)\left(7^{x} - 1\right)}{x^{2}}}{\dfrac{x \log(1 + x)}{x^{2}}}\right]\) ....[As \(x \to 0,\ x^{2} \ne 0\)]

\(= \lim_{x \to 0}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{3^{x} - 1}{x} \times \dfrac{7^{x} - 1}{x}}{\dfrac{\log(1 + x)}{x}}\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{\log 3 \cdot \log 7}{1}\)

.... \(\left[\because \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a^{x} - 1}{x} = \log a,\ \lim_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\log(1 + x)}{x} = 1\right]\)

\(= \log 3 \cdot \log 7\)

solution:
\(\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\frac{ax+b}{cx+d}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{ax+b}{x}}{\dfrac{cx+d}{x}}\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[a + \dfrac{b}{x}\right]}{\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[c + \dfrac{d}{x}\right]}\)

\(= \dfrac{a+0}{c+0}\)  --- as \(x \to \infty\), \(\dfrac{1}{x} \to 0\)

\(= \dfrac{a}{c}\)

subtopic: Limits at Infinity and Infinite Limits
solution:
\(\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\frac{10x^2+5x+3}{5x^2-3x+8}\right]\)

Divide by \(x^2\) to get finite limits of the numerator as well as of the denominator.

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{\dfrac{10x^2+5x+3}{x^2}}{\dfrac{5x^2-3x+8}{x^2}}\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[10 + \dfrac{5}{x} + \dfrac{3}{x^2}\right]}{\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[5 - \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{8}{x^2}\right]}\)

\(= \dfrac{10+0+0}{5-0+0}\)   \(\left(\because \lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{x} = 0\right)\)

\(= \dfrac{10}{5}\)

\(= 2\)

subtopic: Limits at Infinity and Infinite Limits
solution:
\(\lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\sqrt{x^2+3x} - x\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{(\sqrt{x^2+3x} - x)(\sqrt{x^2+3x} + x)}{(\sqrt{x^2+3x} + x)}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{x^2+3x-x^2}{\sqrt{x^2+3x} + x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{3x}{\sqrt{x^2+3x} + x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{3x}{x\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{3}{x}} + x}\right]\)

\(= \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{1 + \dfrac{3}{x}} + 1}\right]\)

\(= \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{1+0} + 1}\)   \(\left(\because \lim_{x \to \infty}\dfrac{1}{x} = 0\right)\)

\(= \dfrac{3}{1+1}\)

\(= \dfrac{3}{2}\)
